clue.text: Grass border with no room to spread

parts.note: grass is slang for cannabis, also called pot
a bound is a boundary or limit

explanation.surface: A lawn edging hemmed in so tightly it cannot grow outwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like a lawn, but it is the drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant whose roots fill its container has no space left to grow, the gardener's term for a cramped pot plant.

clue.text: Evergreen old rowing club

parts.note: Leander is the famous rowing club at Henley-on-Thames

explanation.surface: A veteran rowing club that never ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Leander Club in Henley-on-Thames is one of Britain's oldest rowing clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mediterranean shrub keeps its leaves all year, an example of an evergreen.

clue.text: Menial wets hotel bar, being drunk

indicators.note: drunk means in a disordered state, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A lowly servant soaks the hotel bar while intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody who does the lowest jobs is a menial worker.

clue.text: Not habitually doing nude modelling — won't put in for it

indicators.note: the habit word is put inside the reworked letters
modelling means shaping into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: wont means habit or custom; the apostrophe is ignored

explanation.surface: A model who refuses nude work is not doing it habitually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modelling' rearranges the four letters of 'nude' into UNED, and 'put in' places the habit word inside them; 'for it' just links back to the modelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwonted means unusual or unaccustomed, out of one's habit.

clue.text: Short jacket camouflaged in battle

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Short jacket camouflaged in battle', has no wordplay giving DOUBLET: 'camouflaged in' suggests a hidden word but no printed words contain it; text likely lost in OCR and no scan or search gives the rest.

clue.text: Pretend to influence

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both feigning a manner and having an effect on something.

clue.text: Cut jade

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to chop clumsily; the other is an old tired horse.

clue.text: Help to become a Quaker

parts.note: to become is to be
Quakers are the Religious Society of Friends, so a Quaker is a Friend

explanation.surface: Assisting someone to join the Quakers.
explanation.definitionFit: To befriend someone is to offer them support and assistance.

clue.text: Bad leg concealed from the public

parts.note: food gone bad has gone off
a leg of a journey is one stage of it

explanation.surface: An injured limb is kept out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre, whatever happens in the wings is out of the audience's view.

clue.text: Morally crooked grass

definitions.meaning: a genus of grass used for lawns

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: dishonest in British slang, and a kind of fine grass.

clue.text: Gambler holding foreign currency (marks) is a source of agitation

indicators.note: the gambler's word is held open around the currency and the marks

parts.note: a taker is one who takes up a bet
the rouble is the currency of Russia
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A punter with a pocketful of foreign money stirs up unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' splits the gambler's word after its first letter. M for mark is an abbreviation solvers may not know: the mark was Germany's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stirs up strife is a source of disturbance, a synonym for an agitator.

clue.text: A youth parking admits row over crash in this light

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the first group takes the noise words inside it

parts.note: a lad is a youth
P is the map symbol for parking

indicators.note: in a down clue the first word sits over the second

parts.note: a din is a noisy row
a slam is a loud crash

explanation.surface: A young man parking lets in a noisy collision under some lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' places the noise words before the final P. 'this light' points to the magic lamp with a genie in the Arabian Nights tale, a pantomime favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The magic lamp holding a genie in the Arabian Nights tale is a famous source of light.

clue.text: Commercial outlet for this sort of calendar

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad
a vent is an opening that lets air or steam out

explanation.surface: An advertising outlet sells a particular kind of calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar with little doors counting down the days to Christmas is named after that season.

clue.text: Right of admission to transport

definitions.meaning: to carry away with delight, to enchant

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a way or right in; the verb, stressed on the second syllable, means to enrapture.

clue.text: Commissions about to be backed by foreign cash

indicators.note: by means beside, so the cash comes next
a word turned back to front is backed, so the short word for about runs the other way

parts.note: re means about or concerning
rands are the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: Agents' fees are reversed by payments in foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: Small tasks one is sent to do are jobs one has been commissioned to carry out.

clue.text: Remove spirits from tax to retain soldiers

indicators.note: retain means hold inside, so the tax word keeps the soldiers within it

parts.note: excise is a tax on goods
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Taking the duty off spirits keeps soldiers in drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' looks like drink, given 'tax', but means ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: To exorcise is to drive out demons or ghosts from a person or place.

clue.text: Crystallised preserve came to an end

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in a tin
died means finished or ceased

explanation.surface: A jam that has crystallised has reached the end of its life.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit coated and preserved in sugar becomes glassy with sugar crystals.

clue.text: Wounded Argive, for instance, in distress

definitions.note: the definition is a past form where the entry is the base verb, meaning to hurt or offend

indicators.note: distress here means a damaged, disordered state, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: eg is short for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A Greek soldier, for example, lies hurt and distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: An Argive is a native of Argos, so a Greek in Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to hurt or wrong someone, causing resentment.

clue.text: Keeping rank, retired, and suit REME organisation

indicators.note: organisation means arranging into order, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A retired soldier keeps his rank and wears a REME suit.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps; here only its letters matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor emeritus has retired but keeps an honorary title.

clue.text: Possibly made free with bid to get the full story

indicators.note: possibly made signals the letters could be made into something else

explanation.surface: Someone takes liberties with a bid to learn everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone after a mission is to obtain a complete account.

clue.text: Shed old-fashioned institution

parts.note: out means out of fashion
a house can be an institution, such as a religious house or a workhouse

explanation.surface: Getting rid of an outdated establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A small building separate from the main one, like a garden hut, is a shed.

clue.text: A Continental cheese written up but not in production

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: A European cheese gets reviewed but is not yet made.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not manufactured has never been made.

clue.text: Girl in sports car, a guzzler?

indicators.note: the girl is placed inside the car's letters

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a sports car
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman in a sporty car is a heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as figurative: a gannet is a seabird, so 'guzzler' fits it only as slang for a greedy eater.
explanation.definitionFit: This seabird swallows fish greedily, so its name is British slang for a glutton.

clue.text: Soldiers tried here to cultivate appropriate kind of arts

parts.note: to court someone is to cultivate their favour
martial arts are fighting skills, fitting for soldiers

explanation.surface: A place to train soldiers in combat skills.
explanation.definitionFit: A military tribunal is where service personnel face trial.

clue.text: At first signs of unrest, gungho lout, youth, may be threatening

indicators.note: first signs means the initial letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A gung-ho young thug at the start of unrest may be menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly mood or situation is one that is hostile and menacing.

clue.text: Book exerts influence

definitions.meaning: a book of the New Testament, telling of the apostles
has an effect, as a drug that works on the body

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a biblical book's name; the other is a verb for having an effect.

clue.text: A sound margin with which to market greens, say

indicators.note: say signals the words are spoken, so their sound gives the entry

parts.note: to market is to sell, and greens are veg

explanation.surface: A grocer's sturdy edge for selling vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' in the definition means firm and fray-proof, not a homophone signal; 'say' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven edge that stops cloth fraying is a strong, finished border.

clue.text: You'll not be at a loss to write such a reply

definitions.text: You'll not be at a loss to write such a reply

parts.words: You'll not be at a loss to write such a reply
parts.note: a reply sent under a postal arrangement where the recipient pays, so writing back costs you nothing

explanation.definitionFit: Mail sent without a stamp, paid for by the addressee, leaves the replier out of pocket by nothing.
